title: Orquestación y VP RPA + AI Analyst
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S26.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts adjudicated USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S21-S25 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED. S26 must not launder prior labels such as approved, auto, success, validated or human_review into evidence merely by placing them in a DAG.
not_creditable: S22 approval is bound to the exact final draft and recipient set
S23 browser artifact is uniquely persisted and verified
S24 OCR fields are fully provenance-bound and human-reviewed
S25 AI output is baseline-beating, typed, grounded or actually human-approved

roadmap_expectation.T1: orquestación con tasks/flows/DAG, estados, límites, metadata y schedules
roadmap_expectation.T2: checkpoints, retry/backoff, dead-letter, idempotencia, concurrencia y rollback
roadmap_expectation.T3: revisión humana de análisis/reporte/destinatario con aprobación, rechazo, edición y auditoría
roadmap_expectation.T4: SLO/alerts/runbook y validación E2E, seguridad, costo y métricas de valor
roadmap_expectation.gate: VP RPA + AI Analyst integrado con evidencia reproducible, recuperación de fallas y promoción N2 solo si CP-N2-A/B/C, regresión S14-S26 y CF-2 pasan

live_site.evidence: Public page exposes Section 26 'VP RPA + AI Analyst' and the same tagline promising evidence per state and failure recovery. Render-only defects were not invented.

checks: topo([('a','b'),('b','a')]) returns [] instead of an explicit cycle failure; adding a disconnected root returns a partial order ['root','x'] while silently dropping the cyclic component.
build_run_meta('r',100) returns api_rpm=100 even though prose says >60 blocks schedule; no preflight is implemented.
write_report('r1','v1'); write_report('r1','v2') leaves v2, disproving the create-once/idempotency claim.
rollback('r1') replaces the report record with {'status':'superseded'}, deleting the original report body it claims to preserve.
A review queue containing status='rejected' has pending_count 0 and therefore all_clear=True.
act(...,'reject',...,reason=None) succeeds and audit records omit ts, contradicting the stated audit contract and reject gate.
e2e_vp() manufactures success for all seven steps plus n2_regression='pass', cost_tokens=1200, fraud_labels=0 and value_minutes_saved_est=45 without running any step or test.

external_research.source: AWS Well-Architected REL05-BP03 / AWS Architecture Blog
external_research.finding: Retries should be bounded and use exponential backoff with jitter; retries add load and should be used where operations are safe/idempotent and errors are transient.
Robust idempotency uses persistent records, payload-derived keys, INPROGRESS/COMPLETE states and concurrency locking; an in-memory dict assignment is not an idempotency guarantee.
A DLQ is operational state with retry/redrive policy, retention, monitoring and explicit redrive behavior, not merely a list containing owner/reason.
SLOs require a defined user-relevant SLI, target, measurement window and reaction/error-budget policy; a threshold name alone is incomplete.

findings.evidence: Opening/reference and E2E treat prior ingest/report/OCR/AI pieces as working inputs although S21-S25 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.attack: Orchestration can launder false-green labels from earlier sections into a final success artifact.
findings.defense: An integrator must compose prior modules.
findings.impact: The capstone can promote a run whose source, approval, OCR or AI evidence was never trustworthy.
findings.repair: Require a versioned handoff manifest and revalidate every upstream artifact/hash/review state before the DAG can mark a node ready.

findings.evidence: Canonical path is report → approve → draft_email; S22 requires approval bound to exact draft/message/recipients.
findings.attack: A human cannot approve the exact email draft before that draft exists.
findings.defense: The S26 approve node may intend approval of analysis/report/recipient rather than the final email.
findings.impact: The graph conflates pre-draft business review with final draft approval and loses the safety contract inherited from S22.
findings.repair: Model distinct gates: analysis/report/recipient approvals → create draft → final draft/recipient approval bound to draft hash; never treat the first gate as final email approval.

findings.evidence: Opening says an exhausted timeout usually heals itself and deserves retry.
findings.attack: A timeout can occur after a side effect committed; blind retry can duplicate exports/drafts/writes.
findings.defense: The paragraph later says steps should be idempotent.
findings.impact: Learner receives an unsafe default retry heuristic before idempotency is actually established.
findings.repair: Classify timeout as outcome-unknown; retry only after idempotency/postcondition verification or for explicitly side-effect-free operations.

findings.evidence: topo() returns order without checking len(order)==len(nodes).
findings.attack: A cyclic component is silently omitted; a partially cyclic graph returns a plausible partial order.
findings.defense: A fully cyclic graph returns an empty list and therefore might not start.
findings.impact: The learner can mistake incomplete scheduling for successful DAG validation.
findings.repair: After Kahn traversal, raise a typed CycleError unless every node was emitted; add full-cycle and partial-cycle negative fixtures.

findings.evidence: Theory promises pending/running/success/failed/skipped, global flow state, timestamp and run_id per node; code only returns node names.
findings.attack: No state transition, timestamp, skip rule, dependency failure or global flow status is executable.
findings.defense: The example focuses narrowly on topological order.
findings.impact: Outcome 'tasks/flows/DAG con estados' is not demonstrated by theory code.
findings.repair: Add a node-state record with allowed transitions, timestamps, run_id, dependency outcome and explicit skipped semantics.

findings.evidence: topo() seeds deque from a set of zero-indegree nodes.
findings.attack: With multiple roots, order can vary with hash iteration rather than a documented tie-break, weakening reproducibility.
findings.defense: The canonical seven-step chain has one root.
findings.impact: The generic helper is less deterministic than the surrounding reproducibility claims.
findings.repair: Use a stable ordered node registry or heap/sorted tie-break and state that multiple valid topological orders may exist.

findings.evidence: Prose calls run_id, trigger, git_sha and data_cutoff immutable; build_run_meta omits git_sha, hardcodes trigger/manual and returns a mutable dict.
findings.attack: The object cannot prove code version or immutable start snapshot and can be modified after creation.
findings.defense: It is a didactic metadata sketch.
findings.impact: run_id cannot reliably join evidence across versions/reprocessing.
findings.repair: Include git_sha/config/schema/source hashes/trigger/data_cutoff and freeze or hash the canonical run manifest; create a new run on any change.

findings.evidence: api_rpm and max_parallel_tasks are dictionary values; prose says api_rpm>60 blocks schedule, but no preflight/limiter exists.
findings.attack: build_run_meta('r',100) succeeds and nothing enforces rate/concurrency.
findings.defense: The section may intend configuration before a later runner.
findings.impact: Learner can confuse declaring a limit with enforcing one.
findings.repair: Implement validation plus an actual semaphore/token-bucket/adaptor limit and a negative fixture proving >60 cannot enable the schedule.

findings.evidence: Cron and timezone are printed strings; disable_schedule/drain are prose only.
findings.attack: No scheduler state, timezone binding, enable/disable action or drain behavior is demonstrated.
findings.defense: A conceptual cron example is legitimate at this level.
findings.impact: Outcome 'configurar schedules' is overclaimed as operational capability.
findings.repair: Label the string as schedule specification and add a small state machine or real approved scheduler adapter demonstrating enable/disable/drain.

findings.evidence: T2-A acknowledges its set dies with the process; the integrated E2E never uses the promised JSON/persistent checkpoint.
findings.attack: The section's failure-recovery promise is not demonstrated across process restart.
findings.defense: The paragraph correctly explains the limitation.
findings.impact: A correct warning is not evidence that the gate was met.
findings.repair: Persist checkpoints atomically outside process, kill/restart the runner, and prove already-completed work is not repeated.

findings.evidence: backoff_sleep_ms computes delays, but process_with_dlq never sleeps/uses them and has no jitter.
findings.attack: The retry loop is immediate despite claiming retry with backoff; synchronized retries can amplify load.
findings.defense: The numeric formula is taught separately.
findings.impact: The executable behavior contradicts the resiliency mechanism being taught.
findings.repair: Inject a sleeper, use capped exponential backoff plus jitter, persist attempt timing and test with deterministic seeded jitter.

findings.evidence: process_with_dlq receives flaky_ids rather than typed provider/data/configuration failures.
findings.attack: No code demonstrates 'retry transient, do not retry invalid schema'.
findings.defense: flaky_ids simplifies deterministic labs.
findings.impact: The central decision boundary of retry policy is absent.
findings.repair: Classify errors explicitly and route transient/provider errors to bounded retry, permanent data/config errors to review/DLQ without retry.

findings.evidence: DLQ item stores id/reason/owner only; prose/callout promise owner and SLA and the section discusses operation.
findings.attack: No SLA, run_id, payload hash, first/last failure, retry history, retention, alert or redrive path is modeled.
findings.defense: A minimal list is sufficient to introduce the concept.
findings.impact: DLQ can still become the silent graveyard the text warns against.
findings.repair: Define a DLQ record contract with lineage, attempts, timestamps, owner, SLA, status and controlled redrive/reject workflow.

findings.evidence: write_report and write_draft assign directly into store[run_id].
findings.attack: A second call with the same key overwrites the first body; runtime check v1→v2 leaves v2.
findings.defense: A dictionary prevents duplicate keys.
findings.impact: Duplicate keys are not idempotency when payload changes silently replace prior state.
findings.repair: Use an atomic create-once record with payload hash/status; same key+same payload returns stored result, same key+different payload fails.

findings.evidence: Code keys report/draft only by run_id while prose names (run_id, entity_id).
findings.attack: Different entities or artifact versions inside one run collide and payload/config version is not checked.
findings.defense: The lab creates one report per run.
findings.impact: The abstraction will not safely generalize to the concurrent/entity-level system it claims to teach.
findings.repair: Canonical key must include operation + run + entity/artifact + immutable payload/config/schema hash, persisted atomically.

findings.evidence: Prose describes locked flag/lease TTL; theory code contains no lock or concurrent execution.
findings.attack: Nothing prevents two workers from passing a check and writing simultaneously.
findings.defense: Concurrency implementation is deferred conceptually to production.
findings.impact: Learning outcome 'garantizar concurrencia' is unsupported.
findings.repair: Demonstrate atomic acquire/lease/expiry and simultaneous-worker negative test; avoid check-then-set races.

findings.evidence: rollback replaces {'body':body,'status':'active'} with {'status':'superseded'}.
findings.attack: The original report body disappears although prose explicitly says not to delete it from defense history.
findings.defense: The record key remains.
findings.impact: The compensation destroys evidence needed for audit/review.
findings.repair: Preserve immutable artifact/version/body/hash and append a superseded status/event rather than replacing the record.

findings.evidence: rollback pop() deletes the draft entirely.
findings.attack: A compensated draft vanishes, preventing reconstruction of what was generated and why it was withdrawn.
findings.defense: Removing an unsent draft can be a valid compensation.
findings.impact: Operational cleanup is confused with audit deletion.
findings.repair: Delete provider-side mutable draft if needed but retain an immutable hashed snapshot/status=canceled in the audit store.

findings.evidence: all_clear is true whenever no item has status='pending'.
findings.attack: A rejected/error/needs_revision artifact yields pending=0 and can open the gate.
findings.defense: Current fixture contains only pending items.
findings.impact: The core human gate can fail open under non-happy statuses.
findings.repair: Require exact approved state for the exact required artifact/version in all three queues; every other terminal/intermediate state blocks.

findings.evidence: Paragraph says analysis=1, report=1, recipient=0; code/output use recipient=1.
findings.attack: The explanatory case and executable case are different while presented as the same case.
findings.defense: Both correctly result in blocked/all_clear False.
findings.impact: Learner cannot reliably trace prose to output.
findings.repair: Use one fixture consistently and include the zero-recipient case if that is the intended teaching point.

findings.evidence: ai_assist is treated as a pipeline node whose output feeds report; S25 audit found ungrounded/schema-invalid outputs and no baseline promotion gate.
findings.attack: S26 does not revalidate model revision, typed schema, evidence ids or candidate-vs-baseline status before consuming it.
findings.defense: S26 says AI only proposes and human review follows.
findings.impact: Human review is used as a blanket substitute for machine-contract validation.
findings.repair: Before report state can be ready, validate S25 output against immutable model/config/schema/evidence lineage and fail closed on invalid/ungrounded output.

findings.evidence: Prose requires {action,actor,ts,reason?}; act() omits ts.
findings.attack: Decision ordering and timing cannot be reconstructed reliably.
findings.defense: List order preserves local call order.
findings.impact: The audit contract is materially incomplete.
findings.repair: Generate timezone-aware immutable timestamp plus run_id/artifact_version and persist it append-only.

findings.evidence: Callout says reject without reason is rejected at API; act(...,'reject',reason=None) succeeds.
findings.attack: The code contradicts the stated mandatory rejection reason.
findings.defense: No reject call appears in the happy-path example.
findings.impact: Runbook routing cannot rely on reasons being present.
findings.repair: Validate allowed actions and require nonblank reason/reason_code for reject/edit where policy requires it.

findings.evidence: Prose says edit versions 1→2 without deleting history; act() stores only an action record and no content/version/hash.
findings.attack: There is no edited artifact version to review or bind approval to.
findings.defense: The audit event records that an edit happened.
findings.impact: Approval can refer ambiguously to pre- or post-edit content.
findings.repair: Store immutable artifact versions; edit creates v+1 with parent hash, and approval names the exact version/hash.

findings.evidence: act() accepts arbitrary action/actor and artifact id; no role authorization or artifact hash/version binding exists.
findings.attack: Any synthetic actor can approve any id and the same actor could create/edit/approve without policy checks.
findings.defense: Actors are synthetic because the lab avoids PII.
findings.impact: 'Human approval' is merely a label, not an authorized, attributable control.
findings.repair: Resolve authorized reviewer roles, enforce separation where required and bind decision to exact run/artifact/version/recipient set.

findings.evidence: audit is a normal mutable in-memory Python list.
findings.attack: Entries can be edited/deleted and disappear on process exit; append-only is asserted rather than enforced.
findings.defense: The example itself only calls append.
findings.impact: The learner can mistake usage convention for storage invariant.
findings.repair: Teach append-only as an invariant backed by persistent event records/hashes or clearly label the list as a non-enforcing simulation.

findings.evidence: Prose says success_rate≥0.95 diario; code names success_rate_7d.
findings.attack: Daily and rolling-seven-day objectives are different operational contracts.
findings.defense: Both use the same illustrative threshold.
findings.impact: Alert behavior cannot be reproduced from the stated SLO.
findings.repair: Choose one window and encode numerator, denominator, window and evaluation cadence consistently.

findings.evidence: success_rate_7d and p95_duration_min have no event population/eligibility definition or error-budget/reaction policy.
findings.attack: A numeric target without SLI semantics can be gamed by skipped/rejected runs or changing denominators.
findings.defense: The section calls the SLO synthetic.
findings.impact: Learner sees alert arithmetic rather than a defendable service objective.
findings.repair: Define eligible runs, success predicate, window, measurement point, target, error budget and response before calculating alerts.

findings.evidence: Runbook orders disable_schedule → drain → page oncall and defines drain as emptying workers before notification.
findings.attack: A drain can stall; delaying notification until after completion can hide a P0 and mixes mitigation with escalation.
findings.defense: For a small synthetic batch the sequence may finish quickly.
findings.impact: The learner gets an unsafe universal incident sequence.
findings.repair: Detect/page immediately according to severity, quiesce new work, drain/cancel with timeout and explicit side-effect policy, then diagnose/recover.

findings.evidence: e2e_vp assigns 'success' to every step without executing any step.
findings.attack: It manufactures exactly the evidence the promotion gate is supposed to prove.
findings.defense: It can be read as the shape of an evidence package.
findings.impact: A learner can emit green E2E while nothing ran.
findings.repair: Run actual section adapters/stubs with assertions, collect their returned artifact hashes/states and derive success from observed results only.

findings.evidence: n2_regression is hardcoded to 'pass'; CP-N2-A/B/C and CF-2 are not executed or referenced by artifact.
findings.attack: Promotion evidence is a literal string, despite text saying real, not planned.
findings.defense: The snippet demonstrates package fields.
findings.impact: The strongest gate in the section is self-certified.
findings.repair: Load signed/tested regression result manifests with test counts/commit/source hashes and refuse promotion if any required suite is missing or failed.

findings.evidence: fraud_labels=0 is assigned; secrets-outside-repo and least scopes are prose only.
findings.attack: No scan/query proves absence of forbidden labels/secrets or scope violations.
findings.defense: The lab uses synthetic data and no real providers.
findings.impact: Security/control compliance is represented by literals instead of checks.
findings.repair: Derive fraud-label count from emitted artifacts, scan fixtures/logs for forbidden data/secrets and validate effective provider/tool permissions where relevant.

findings.evidence: cost_tokens=1200 and value_minutes_saved_est=45 are hardcoded; no model price, RPA duration, budget or manual baseline measurement is used.
findings.attack: The tagline/job relevance promise bounded cost and value evidence, but the package contains invented numbers.
findings.defense: The paragraph labels minutes saved as an estimate, not financial promise.
findings.impact: Learner is taught to populate KPI fields rather than measure/derive them.
findings.repair: Calculate tokens from observed calls with model/version pricing snapshot; measure RPA/manual baseline on declared fixtures and label uncertainty/sample size.

findings.evidence: Paragraph says any failed step makes E2E false; e2e_vp has no failure input/path and always returns success.
findings.attack: The gate never demonstrates recovery, blocking or fail-closed behavior under failure.
findings.defense: Failure handling is discussed in T2.
findings.impact: Section closes with only a manufactured happy path despite claiming recovery evidence.
findings.repair: Add injected failures before/after side effects, process restart, retry exhaustion, human reject and verify final E2E/promotion is false or recovered with evidence.

findings.evidence: No integrated record links S21 report/S22 approvals/S23 download/S24 OCR/S25 model output to S26 review/draft by hashes and versions.
findings.attack: run_id alone cannot prove which exact artifact/model/reviewer decision produced the final draft.
findings.defense: The narrative repeatedly names a common VP pipeline.
findings.impact: The integrator loses the provenance needed to defend the final outcome.
findings.repair: Persist one lineage graph/manifest carrying immutable artifact hashes, schema/model revisions, reviewer decisions and parent-child edges through every node.

false_positives_rejected: Using a DAG without Prefect/Airflow is not itself a defect; a correct standard-library model can teach the contract.
A dead-letter queue is not inherently bad for FIFO or ordered work; the defect here is incomplete operational semantics, not DLQ existence.
The statement matching/score is not fraud was retained; no evidence supports treating it as a defect.
A synthetic SLO target is acceptable for a lab if its SLI/window/reaction are explicit; the problem is the inconsistent/undefined contract, not the value 0.95 alone.
The section does not send real email in theory; the safety defect is approval/draft ordering and false evidence, not actual unauthorized sending.

USABLE: DAG dependencies are a useful orchestration model
checkpoint and idempotency are distinct concepts
permanent data/config errors should not be retried like transient provider failures
DLQ requires human ownership rather than silent deletion
matching/OCR evidence is not a fraud verdict
compensation is not identical to an ACID rollback
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: returning a partial topological order means the DAG is valid
an in-memory locked flag guarantees concurrency safety
a list is append-only because code only calls append
approval before creating the email draft satisfies final draft approval
